key_insight: MORL-A2C turns food recommendation into a sequential reranking policy that meaningfully boosts health alignment while preserving reasonable recommendation quality.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how reinforcement learning can be layered on top of frozen graph-based embeddings to control multi-objective tradeoffs in recommender systems.
method: Frozen GNN embeddings initialize item/user representations.
A2C reranks top-K candidates with a scalarized relevance/health reward.
Behavior cloning warm-starts the policy from a dot-product ranker.
evidence_signal: On the macro-nutrient benchmark, health alignment improved sharply (H-Score@20: 46.05% to 69.57%) while ranking quality decreased modestly (Recall@20: 25.64% to 23.61%, NDCG@20: 23.52% to 20.64%).
watch_item: Results depend on a corrected baseline after fixing an evaluation bug in MOPI-HFRS, so absolute gains should be interpreted relative to that revised pipeline.
paper_title: MORL-A2C: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Reranker for Optimizing Healthiness in MOPI-HFRS
